info.title: Ivora Platform API
info.description:
The Ivora API for tenant charger management, charging, billing and payment adapters.

### Start here

1. Sign in to the [Ivora dashboard](https://platform.ivoracharge.co). Your CSMS tenant is assigned automatically. In your project, open **Developers → API keys** and create a key with the scopes your application needs; station and billing keys bind to your tenant automatically.
2. Send the key from your server as `Authorization: Bearer iv_test_…`. A preproduction Ivora sign-in (session) token also works.
3. Call `GET /v1/access` (under **Access and API keys** in the API reference, where the portal's Try it console calls it with your `iv_test_…` key), then use your tenant ID in the station, billing and payment routes. For onboarding outside the dashboard, call `POST /v1/me/tenant` with your Ivora sign-in (session) token first. Repeating this call returns the same assignment. Existing CSMS grants retain their current permissions.
4. The [API reference](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/api) lists each operation's scopes, parameters, responses and samples.

### Choose a workflow

Start with the [settlement flow comparison](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/settlement)
and [architecture diagrams](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/getting-started/architecture).
The guides distinguish managed payments, application-managed processors, free charging and test charging on the OCPP bench. **External charging sessions**
allow your backend to integrate its own processor now. Self-service managed-adapter
registration remains planned.

Business profiles, free-charging eligibility/passwords, QR cards and checkout
presentation belong to the consuming application and its database. The shared
API handles charger operations, trusted usage and billing support. It also keeps
the QR a charger's own screen shows as desired state; your application chooses
that URL and serves its page.

| Task | Reference sections | Order of calls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Register a charger | Locations → Stations | Create location → register station (both return the resource) → set connection credentials → read connector state |
| Show a QR on a charger screen | Stations → Charger displays | Read the station's `display` field → set each EVSE's display → watch `delivery.state` or `display.delivery_changed`; print the QR where the state is `unsupported` |
| Stop polling | Webhooks and events | Register an HTTPS endpoint → verify the signed test delivery → consume operation, session, bill and display events |
| Paid charging | Tariffs and bills → Payments → Charging and operations | Create bill → authorize payment → follow checkout → confirm authorization → start bill → observe transaction → stop → finalize bill → capture |
| Application-managed processor | External charging sessions | Authorize in your backend → create session → attest funding/start → observe/stop → finalize → capture in your backend → optionally report outcome |
| Release or refund | Payments | Release an unused authorization; refund a captured payment |
| Try without hardware | Workspaces → Test charging | Create workspace → start a test session on an OCPP bench charger → watch its live meter and running cost → stop and settle the real bill |

Every bill is a `csms` bill: it is finalized from a completed `transaction_id`, never from caller-supplied energy. To try payments without your own hardware, use a workspace test session on the OCPP bench where `/v1/capabilities` reports `ocpp_bench`.

### Access, units and retries

- Keep tenant API keys on your application server. Your app controls host/guest permissions and bookings within its granted fleet.
- Station reads need `stations:read`; provisioning and charger displays need `stations:write`; commands need `stations:control`. A station's redacted OCPP message log needs `stations:diagnostics`, which only keys created with it hold and viewers never do. Bills and payments use `billing:read` / `billing:write`; tariffs are read with `billing:read`, and creating, changing or archiving one, or choosing the tariff of a connector, location or project, needs `tariffs:write`. Bill start also needs `stations:control`. External session creation/start opts in with `settlement:write`; reporting requires that scope and never executes a payment. RFID tokens use `tokens:read` / `tokens:write` (tenant-admin). Overview statistics (`/stats`) need `stations:read`; their revenue fields also need `billing:read`. Key management requires a signed-in workspace owner.
- Charging/billing writes that declare **Idempotency-Key** require 8–128 printable characters. Generate a unique key per operation and reuse it with the same body after a timeout.
- Creating a location, station or tariff returns **201 with the resource and its ID**; add `external_reference` to find it by your own identifier. Charger-bound writes return a **202 operation**: poll it, or subscribe to `operation.completed` under **Webhooks and events**. Reconcile an `unknown` charger outcome before issuing another command. Unknown payment operations older than 23 hours require operator reconciliation.
- Errors are `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"}}` with stable codes such as `station_offline` or `idempotency_key_reused`; rejected operations repeat the shape in `result.error`.
- Versions are dates. This contract is version **2026-10-15** (`info.version`), served under the path major `/v1`; the supported versions are 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-15. Every response carries `Ivora-Version` with the version applied. Requests may send `Ivora-Version: 2026-10-15`; an unknown value answers `400 invalid_api_version` listing the supported versions. API keys and webhook endpoints show the version they are pinned to (`api_version`), and webhook deliveries carry it in `Ivora-Version`. Changes are additive by default; a breaking change ships only as a new dated version, announced in the [changelog](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/changelog) at least six months before the older version or a deprecated field sunsets. Deprecated routes answer with `Deprecation`, `Sunset` and a `Link` to the changelog.
- Core energy is **kWh** and every energy field also carries integer **`energy_wh`**; charger displays and meter samples report OCPP 1.6 registers in **Wh**; tariff and payment amounts are integer **minor currency units**. Bills fix the tariff and final amount; payment clients cannot choose a different capture amount.

The first payment adapter supports USD and CAD test cards (the bill's currency), authorization, capture, release and full refund. Self-service payment provider registration and marketplace payouts are not available.

[Workflow guides](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides) · [Download OpenAPI](https://api.ivoracharge.co/openapi.json)

get.summary: Health
Public Config
List the supported currencies
get.description: Public: the currencies tariffs, bills and projects accept, with each one's ISO 4217 decimals (exponent) and card payment limits in minor units. Any other code returns currency_unsupported. A bill is in its tariff's currency; there is no conversion between currencies. Managed card payments take USD; settle bills in another currency through an external charging session.

get.summary: List the tax presets
get.description: Public: editable starting points for a location's tax lines (PUT .../locations/{location_id}/tax with preset and confirm_preset true): Canada's provinces and territories (GST, HST, PST, QST, RST) and the US states with a per-kWh EV charging excise. Ivora does not guarantee their legal correctness: the operator is the seller, checks what applies and files the tax. US sales tax depends on state, county and city and has no preset.

Read what smart charging the charger reported
get.description: From the configuration the charging core recorded, never a live read: OCPP 1.6 SupportedFeatureProfiles, ChargeProfileMaxStackLevel, ChargingScheduleAllowedChargingRateUnit, ChargingScheduleMaxPeriods and MaxChargingProfilesInstalled; OCPP 2.0.1/2.1 SmartChargingCtrlr Enabled, Available, RateUnit, ProfileStackLevel, PeriodsPerSchedule and Entries. Unreported values are null; refresh them with POST .../configuration/refresh. Profile writes refuse what the charger reported it cannot take. Requires stations:read.

get.summary: List the station's charging profiles
get.description: The profiles set through this API, oldest first, with their state: pending (the charger has not answered), accepted, rejected (by the charger, charger_status, or the charging core, error), unknown, no_reply, cleared, replaced (OCPP 1.6: a later profile took the same purpose, connector and stack level) or ended (its session is over). Profiles the charger holds from elsewhere are not listed; GET a composite schedule for what the charger actually applies. Paginate with after=next_cursor. Requires stations:read.

post.summary: Set a charging profile (SetChargingProfile)
post.description: OCPP 1.6 SetChargingProfile (ChargePointMaxProfile, TxDefaultProfile, TxProfile) or OCPP 2.0.1/2.1 SetChargingProfile (ChargingStationMaxProfile, TxDefaultProfile, TxProfile). purpose charger_max caps the whole station, tx_default every new session on the station or one connector, session one active transaction. unit is W or A; give periods, or time-of-use windows with time_zone and default_limit (a daily recurring schedule). Requires stations:control. result.profile_id names the profile; its state follows the charger's answer (charging_profile.accepted or .rejected webhooks). A refusal by the charging core (OCPP 2.x checks, such as a second profile at the same purpose, EVSE and stack level) rejects the operation with 422 charging_profile_refused and its reason. Offline stations answer station_offline in the rejected operation. result.charger_status carries the charger's answer. Errors: 402 billing_suspended, 402 payment_method_required, 409 smart_charging_unsupported, 409 station_offline, 422 charging_profile_refused, 422 charging_profile_unsupported. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

get.summary: Read one charging profile
get.description: Requires stations:read.

delete.description: Clears the profile by its chargingProfileId. A profile no longer pending or accepted answers 409 charging_profile_inactive, creating no operation. The profile reads cleared once the charger answers Accepted, or Unknown (it held no such profile), with a charging_profile.cleared webhook. Requires stations:control. Errors: 402 billing_suspended, 402 payment_method_required, 409 charging_profile_inactive, 409 station_offline. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

post.summary: Clear the station's charging profiles of a purpose
post.description: ClearChargingProfile by criteria: every profile of purpose on the station, optionally only one connector's (its EVSE on OCPP 2.x) or one stack level, including profiles set outside this API. result.profile_ids lists the API's profiles it covers; they read cleared once the charger answers Accepted or Unknown. Requires stations:control. Errors: 402 billing_suspended, 402 payment_method_required, 409 station_offline. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

post.summary: Ask the charger for its composite schedule (GetCompositeSchedule)
post.description: The limits the charger will actually apply from now for duration_seconds, every profile combined (its own and other systems' too). result.schedule holds them once the charger answers: start_at, duration_seconds, unit and periods (start_offset_seconds, limit, number_phases), null when it answers Rejected. connector_id narrows it to one connector (its EVSE on OCPP 2.x). It changes nothing on the charger, so it is a read: requires stations:read (viewers too), takes an Idempotency-Key like every operation and is never refused for the usage fee. Errors: 409 station_offline. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

put.summary: Cap a running session's power or current
put.description: Sets a session profile (TxProfile) with one period of limit in unit for the active transaction, from the start of the session. Setting it again changes the cap: OCPP 1.6 replaces the earlier one at the same stack level; on OCPP 2.x the new cap goes one stack level above the session's earlier ones, which the higher level overrides; once that would pass the charger's reported highest stack level it answers 409 charging_limit_stack_full (details.stack_level, details.max_stack_level) before anything is sent: remove the cap, then set it again. A limit of 0 pauses the session until the cap changes or is removed. The cap ends with the transaction. result.profile_id names the profile on the station; an unknown transaction answers 404 transaction_not_found and an ended one a rejected operation (transaction_ended). Requires stations:control. Errors: 402 billing_suspended, 402 payment_method_required, 404 transaction_not_found, 409 charging_limit_stack_full, 409 smart_charging_unsupported, 409 transaction_ended, 422 charging_profile_unsupported. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

delete.description: ClearChargingProfile of every session profile (TxProfile) on the transaction's connector (OCPP 1.6) or EVSE (OCPP 2.x): the session continues under the station's tx_default and charger_max profiles. Requires stations:control. Errors: 402 billing_suspended, 402 payment_method_required, 409 station_offline. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

post.summary: Register a station and return it
post.description: Synchronous: the response is the station with its resource ID, connectors and default connection_url. Supply name, a globally unique OCPP connection name, or charger_id, the charger's own identity, unique within the project. Projects have per-project charger URLs by default where offered (409 project_urls_disabled where they are off): the charger then connects at its project URL, such as wss://ocpp.ivoracharge.co/18/CP001, and name is p<tenant_id>-<charger_id>. A taken name or charger ID returns station_name_taken. Idempotency-Key replays return the same station; the journal guarantees one registration per key. A 503 outcome_unknown means the core did not answer: list stations by name, charger_id or external_reference before retrying with a new key. When a charger_id registration replaces a global station of the same name in this project (the move to project URLs), the new station copies its EVSEs, connectors (type, power, physical reference; connectors then ignores the request) and each connector's tariff; the old station is only read. The first response carries warnings (layout_not_copied if the old station could not be read, layout_differs, connectors_without_tariff, tariff_archived when a copied tariff is archived; it is still copied); a replay answers without them. Registration does not connect hardware; set credentials next. Errors: 402 billing_suspended, 402 payment_method_required, 409 external_reference_taken, 409 project_urls_disabled, 409 request_in_progress, 409 self_serve_charger_cap, 409 station_name_taken, 503 outcome_unknown. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

get.summary: Read station and connector state

delete.summary: Delete a station that never charged
delete.description: Synchronous. Deletes the station, its EVSEs and connectors when it has no transactions; a connected station is disconnected first. Stations with charging history return 409 station_has_history and stay in inventory (detach them in your application instead); an active transaction returns 409 transaction_active; a station in shadow mode 409 station_shadow. Replays with the same Idempotency-Key return the same result.

patch.summary: Edit a station's name, location or metadata
patch.description: Changes only the supplied fields; the operation's result is the updated station. location_id moves the station to another location of this tenant. floor_level, latitude and longitude (together), parking_restrictions and capabilities describe it (as OCPI publishes them); a list replaces the stored one. vendor, model and serial are read-only: the charger reports them in its BootNotification. name renames the OCPP connection name only while the charger has never connected (409 station_connected afterwards, since it is the charger's OCPP identity; register a new station instead): the charger then connects at the new connection_url, and a password set earlier moves with it. charger_id does the same with a per-project charger ID, in a project with per-project charger URLs. A name in use returns station_name_taken. metadata merges into the station's metadata (a key sent as "" or null is deleted); bills, charging sessions and transactions keep the metadata they snapshot when they started. No charger message is sent. Replays with the same Idempotency-Key return the same operation.

post.summary: Decommission a station
post.description: Flags a charger the owner dropped for good. Monitoring, alerts, charger events and fleet counts skip it, so its being offline or refused is expected, and station reads report decommissioned true. It takes no new sessions: the start command, bill creation, bill and charging-session starts and checkout answer 409 station_decommissioned; a running session finishes normally and can still be stopped. Its history, sessions and bills stay, and nothing is sent to the charger. It is not a delete (DELETE the station for that). name must be the station's connection name (409 station_name_mismatch, details.name); reason is kept with the flag. Emits station.decommissioned. Needs stations:admin (team owners and admins, Ivora staff, and API keys created with it). Synchronous and idempotent: a repeat changes nothing and answers changed false, and only a change emits a webhook. Audit-logged with the caller. Ivora staff can set and clear the same flag; the station's tenant then receives the same events. Errors: 404 station_not_found, 409 station_name_mismatch. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

delete.description: Clears the decommissioned flag: the station is monitored again and takes new sessions. Emits station.recommissioned. Needs stations:admin (team owners and admins, Ivora staff, and API keys created with it). Synchronous and idempotent: a repeat changes nothing and answers changed false, and only a change emits a webhook. Audit-logged with the caller. Ivora staff can set and clear the same flag; the station's tenant then receives the same events. Errors: 404 station_not_found. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

post.summary: Add an EVSE with its connectors
post.description: Synchronous: the response is the EVSE with its connectors' resource IDs. Connectors take the next OCPP 1.6 connector numbers on the station and are numbered 1, 2, ... on the EVSE; type, format, power_type, max_power_w (W), max_amperage_a (A) and max_voltage_v (V) describe each. A taken evse_number, including that of a removed EVSE transactions keep, returns 409 evse_number_taken. Assign tariffs as for any connector. No charger message is sent: the charger reports its own EVSEs. Replays with the same Idempotency-Key return the same result.

put.summary: Set the station's OCPP connection password
put.description: Offline stations store the password for their next connection (result.applied = stored). Connected OCPP 2.0.1/2.1 stations receive it over OCPP and it is stored once accepted (result.applied = pushed). Connected OCPP 1.6 stations receive it as ChangeConfiguration AuthorizationKey; the API waits up to 10 seconds for the charger's answer and stores the password only when the charger took it. Accepted: result.applied = pushed. RebootRequired: result.applied = reboot_required, also stored, since the charger's next connection after it reboots uses the new password. Either way the charger's current connection stays up and the new password takes effect when it reconnects; result.note says so and result.charger_status carries the charger's answer. Rejected, NotSupported or a CALLERROR: the operation is rejected with 409 password_rejected (error.details.applied = rejected or not_supported) and the old password stays. No answer in time: status unknown with 502 password_unconfirmed (details.applied = unconfirmed); the old password stays stored. The charger may still have taken the new one, so repeat the request with the same password and a new Idempotency-Key before it reconnects. Only one 1.6 push per station runs at a time: another one still waiting for the charger answers 409 request_in_progress and sends nothing. The password is never returned, logged or kept in the operation, and the OCPP message log shows it as [redacted]. Offline and new stations need stations:write (result.applied = stored). Pushing to a connected charger is a configuration change on the charger and needs stations:admin (team owners and admins, Ivora staff, and API keys created with it): stations:write alone answers 403 stations_admin_required before any operation is created (the Idempotency-Key stays unused); set it while the charger is offline instead. A password stored as the charger connects takes effect on its next connection. At most 5 changes per station per hour, whoever asks: 429 credentials_rate_limited with Retry-After after that; a replay with the same Idempotency-Key is not a new change. Each change is in the project's operations (kind station.password) and emits station.credentials_changed, never with the password.

post.summary: Dispatch a charger command (start, stop, reset, unlock, availability or a maintenance command)
post.description: Start is an operator command and does not authorize payment. For paid charging start an authorized bill. A succeeded operation means the adapter replied; observe dispatch response and transactions for charging. Never resend unknown or dispatching operations with a new key. disconnect closes the charger's WebSocket (it normally reconnects by itself). clear_cache clears its authorization cache. transaction_status (OCPP 2.0.1/2.1 GetTransactionStatus, optional transaction_id) reports result.transaction_ongoing and result.messages_in_queue; OCPP 1.6 has no such message and answers 409 command_unsupported. update_firmware (location, optional retrieve_at and retries) asks the charger to download and install firmware; follow it with station.firmware_status events. It answers 409 transaction_active while a transaction is active on the station, since installing usually reboots the charger, unless a signed-in Ivora platform administrator sets force (403 for anyone else). upload_diagnostics (location, optional from, to and retries) asks the charger to upload its diagnostics (OCPP 1.6 GetDiagnostics) or diagnostics log (OCPP 2.x GetLog); follow it with station.diagnostics_status events. location must be https without credentials: the charger itself downloads from or uploads to it, and results repeat it without its query string. start answers 422 token_reserved when the token value is a roaming partner's token in this tenant. clear_cache, transaction_status, update_firmware and upload_diagnostics carry the charger's answer in result.charger_status. Errors: 402 billing_suspended, 402 payment_method_required, 403 forbidden, 409 command_unsupported, 409 station_offline, 409 transaction_active, 422 token_reserved. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

get.summary: Read the station's recorded configuration

Request a fresh report with POST .../configuration/refresh. Sensitive values (passwords, PINs and PUKs, keys, secrets, tokens, Wi-Fi and APN settings) are always null. protected keys (anything but the standard keys every tenant key may change) need stations:admin to change; connection keys also need confirm_connection_change. Paginate with after=next_cursor.

post.summary: Change one configuration key or variable
post.description: OCPP 1.6 ChangeConfiguration ({key, value}) or OCPP 2.0.1/2.1 SetVariables ({component, variable, value}, optional instances, evse_number and attribute_type). Requires stations:control. charger_status is Accepted, RebootRequired (reset the station to apply), Rejected, NotSupported, UnknownComponent or UnknownVariable. Tenants may change the standard OCPP 1.6 keys and OCPP 2.0.1 component/variable pairs, except those that could disconnect the charger from Ivora or weaken its security (security profile, central system URL, identity, network, TLS, certificates, ISO 15118). Every other key, vendor keys included, is protected: refused with 403 configuration_key_protected unless the caller also holds stations:admin (team owners and admins, Ivora staff, and API keys created with it; allow_protected is ignored). A protected key the charger reports read-only is refused with 403 configuration_key_read_only. Connection keys (WebSocketURL, OCPPID, SecurityProfile, the central system URL or charger identity, the OCPP 2.x NetworkConfiguration component and the SecurityCtrlr and OCPPCommCtrlr network variables, and any key named like a URL, host, server, address or identity) are protected and also need confirm_connection_change: true (422 connection_change_unconfirmed otherwise); their result carries connection true and a warning: a wrong value disconnects the charger from Ivora. Sensitive keys (passwords, PINs, keys, secrets, tokens, Wi-Fi and APN settings) are refused for everyone with 403 configuration_key_sensitive (set the station password with PUT .../credentials). The value of a protected key is not repeated in the result. Every change is in the project's operations (kind station.configuration) and emits station.configuration_changed with the key, and the value only for unprotected keys. Errors: 403 configuration_key_protected, 403 configuration_key_read_only, 403 configuration_key_sensitive, 409 station_offline, 422 configuration_address_invalid, 422 configuration_value_too_long, 422 connection_change_unconfirmed. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

The core records the answer; read it with GET .../configuration; result.charger_status is the charger's answer. Requires stations:control. Errors: 409 station_offline. post.summary: Ask the charger to send a message now (TriggerMessage)

A message the station's protocol cannot trigger is refused with 422 trigger_unsupported. connector_id narrows it to one connector. Requires stations:control. charger_status is Accepted, Rejected or NotImplemented; the requested message itself arrives as usual (station events, faults, meter values). Errors: 409 station_offline, 422 trigger_unsupported. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

get.description: The tax lines and price mode bills at this location take; configured false without any (no tax). Errors: 404 location_not_found. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

put.description: Replaces the location's tax configuration: lines (percent, or per_kwh in minor units of the tariff's currency) applied in order, with price_mode tax_exclusive (tariff prices exclude tax; the lines are added) or tax_inclusive (tariff prices include them). Or preset (GET /v1/tax-presets) with confirm_preset true, as an editable starting point. lines [] removes the tax. Ivora computes and prints the lines you configure; you are the seller and are responsible for their legal correctness and for filing the tax. A bill freezes its station's location tax when it is created: a change applies to bills created afterwards, never to an open or final one. Needs stations:admin (team owners and admins, Ivora staff, and API keys created with it). Synchronous; replays with the same Idempotency-Key return the current configuration. Audit-logged with the caller. Errors: 404 location_not_found, 422 tax_invalid, 422 tax_preset_unconfirmed, 422 tax_preset_unknown. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

Connectors with their own tariff keep it. A tariff in another currency than the project's default_currency needs confirm_currency true. The pricing order: a connector's own tariff, else the default tariff of its station's location, else the project's default tariff, else none. A station added later inherits the defaults. A bill freezes its tariff when it is created, so a change never moves an open bill or a running session's price; new bills, quotes and displays use it. Needs stations:write and tariffs:write. Recorded in the audit log with the previous and new tariff. Synchronous; replays with the same Idempotency-Key return the same result. post.description: Synchronous: the response carries the tariff resource ID. Historical tariffs and the independent payment catalog are unchanged. A simple tariff takes rate_minor_per_kwh; a complex one takes elements (OCPI 2.2.1-aligned blocks), optionally tariff_alt_text, rules and time_zone, and its base rate is derived. Invalid or ambiguous elements return 422 tariff_invalid with every problem in details.errors. The simple fields stay kWh-only: a non-zero rate_minor_per_minute or session_fee_minor returns 422. Needs tariffs:write. Replays with the same Idempotency-Key return the same tariff.

get.description: From API version 2026-10-15 the tariff carries its elements, tariff_alt_text, rules and time_zone; earlier versions see the simple fields, is_complex and pricing_summary.

patch.description: Synchronous. Changes only the supplied fields, with the rules of tariff creation, and records a tariff.updated event with each change and the actor. The simple fields are kWh-only: a non-zero rate_minor_per_minute or session_fee_minor returns 422; 0 stores 0. elements replace every element and update the base rate; rate_minor_per_kwh alone on a complex tariff returns 409 tariff_complex. Changing the prices of a tariff whose tariff_alt_text you supplied needs tariff_alt_text (or null for the generated text) in the same request, so drivers never read a stale price. Bills snapshot their tariff when they are created: an open or final bill, and the running cost of a session already billed, keep the old price; new bills and charger displays use the new one. An archived tariff returns 409 tariff_archived. metadata merges into the tariff's metadata (a key sent as "" or null is deleted) and is in tariff.updated's changes when it changed. Needs tariffs:write. Replays with the same Idempotency-Key return the current tariff.

delete.description: Synchronous. The tariff keeps its ID and price for the bills that snapshot it, leaves tariff lists (include_archived=true lists it), takes no more edits and starts no new bill or display (409 tariff_archived). While a station's connector, a charger display or a location's or the project's default tariff uses it, or it is the OCPP bench tariff, it returns 409 tariff_in_use with the connectors, displays and defaults in details. Supply replacement_tariff_id, an active tariff in this tenant, to move those connectors, displays and defaults to it first. Records a tariff.archived event with the actor. The archive is recorded only in this API: the charging core keeps the row and does not know the tariff is archived. Needs tariffs:write. Replays with the same Idempotency-Key return the same result.

A charging session shares its bill's metadata. station_metadata and location_metadata, the snapshot taken when the bill was created, never change. Nothing else on the bill changes. Requires billing:write. Replays with the same Idempotency-Key return the current bill. Errors: 404 bill_not_found, 422 metadata_key_invalid, 422 metadata_too_many_keys, 422 metadata_value_invalid. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

get.summary: Read a bill with its usage and start operation
get.description: Open physical bills with a dispatched start report the matched transaction as usage (ambiguity fails closed); final bills keep a final usage snapshot; progress is the driver-facing step. Reads never finalize or move money. Driver return: while the bill's payment, created with return_surface driver and a return_reference, awaits authorization, a read asks the provider (at most every 2 seconds), and a reader holding billing:write and stations:control starts the charger once, as the start endpoint would, when the authorization is at most 9 minutes old.

post.summary: Calculate the final bill from completed charging usage
post.description: Physical bills require a matching tenant/station/connector/token and completed CSMS transaction. The API reads kWh and calculates integer cents with final half-up rounding. No amount override; final bills never change. Legacy-settled transactions are refused.

post.summary: Start charging after adapter authorization
post.description: Requires billing:write and stations:control. Registers a short-lived charging token, then dispatches once. Poll transactions for actual charging. An unknown operation requires reconciliation, not a new start key. A bill whose driver-return payment was started on a bill read (see Read a bill) answers a new start key with that start operation. An optional body sets one session limit (limit.energy_kwh, or limit.amount_minor with currency at the bill's per-kWh rate): the platform stops the session when it reaches it and reports the stop and any overrun in the bill's limit. A start without a body has no limit. Errors: 422 limit_currency_mismatch, 422 limit_too_large, 422 limit_too_small, 422 limit_unpriced. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

post.summary: Record a billing alert for a bill
post.description: Requires billing:write on the bill's tenant. kind hold_stop: the application stopped charging because usage neared the hold. Recorded once per bill and kind; repeating the call returns the same alert. Alerts never move money.

post.summary: Create an externally funded charging session
post.description: Requires billing:write and settlement:write. Atomically snapshots the tariff and fixes external settlement ownership. Your backend owns checkout, processor credentials and capture. References contain no secrets. One open physical external session per connector; this does not reserve hardware against other CSMS commands. metadata sets the session's own key/value pairs (its bill's); the station's and location's metadata are copied into station_metadata and location_metadata now and never change afterwards. Errors: 402 billing_suspended, 402 payment_method_required, 422 metadata_key_invalid, 422 metadata_too_many_keys, 422 metadata_value_invalid. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

get.summary: Find externally funded sessions
get.description: Repository snapshots only, without hardware reads. Follow GET by session ID for live usage. A stable application_reference recovers a session after a lost creation response. Optional filters combine with AND and run in the query, so cursor pages stay full and stable: status is open (not yet completed or canceled: prepared, starting, charging, stopping, awaiting_bill and reconciliation_required), completed or canceled; station_id and connector_id; from (inclusive) and to (exclusive), ISO 8601 against the creation time, UTC when no offset is given. An unknown status or an unreadable or inverted time range is invalid_request (400). metadata[key]=value matches the session's metadata, station_metadata[key]=value and location_metadata[key]=value its snapshot of the station's and location's metadata, exactly and with AND across keys; a malformed one is invalid_request (400). A station of another tenant matches nothing. Repository snapshots show the last known status, so open lists live sessions too; use GET by ID to observe one. Cursors order by opaque session ID, not time.

get.summary: Observe session usage, bill and reported settlement
get.description: Requires billing:read. Correlates live transactions by tenant, station, connector and private charging token. Reads never dispatch commands, finalize a bill or move money. Multiple matches fail closed. A completed bill stays readable if CSMS is unavailable.

patch.description: Requires billing:write. Synchronous. Merges metadata into the session's metadata (its bill's), during or after the session: a key sent as "" or null is deleted, other keys keep their values. station_metadata and location_metadata, the snapshot taken when the session was created, never change. Nothing else changes and no charger is contacted. Replays with the same Idempotency-Key return the session as it is now. Errors: 404 session_not_found, 422 metadata_key_invalid, 422 metadata_too_many_keys, 422 metadata_value_invalid. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

post.summary: Start using application-confirmed funding
post.description: Requires billing:write, stations:control and settlement:write. funding_confirmed is an application assertion, not verification by Ivora. Registers a 15-minute token and dispatches at most once per session. Poll session state; successful dispatch is not physical start. There is no automatic stop at the external hold amount; set limit (energy_kwh, or amount_minor with currency at the bill's per-kWh rate) and the platform stops the session when it reaches it, reporting the stop and any overrun in bill.limit. Errors: 422 limit_currency_mismatch, 422 limit_too_large, 422 limit_too_small, 422 limit_unpriced. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

post.summary: Stop the transaction belonging to this session
post.description: Requires billing:write and stations:control. Never accepts an arbitrary transaction ID. Unknown or rejected attempts after reservation require operator reconciliation; another key cannot dispatch twice.

post.summary: Finalize trusted usage for external capture
post.description: Requires billing:write. Usage requires the completed transaction ID observed on the session. The result is immutable, in minor units of the bill's currency. Capture it in your backend; Ivora does not call your processor.

post.summary: Cancel a session before any start reservation
post.description: Requires billing:write. Does not release funds. Once start is reserved, a timeout or absent transaction is insufficient evidence to cancel; reconcile the charger and finalize actual usage.

post.summary: Record an external processor outcome without moving money
post.description: Requires settlement:write. Application-reported, never independently verified. Append-only provenance and operation-reference deduplication. Pending/unknown can resolve once to succeeded/failed; terminal results and amounts cannot change. Successful captures cannot exceed the final bill; refunds cannot exceed successful captures. No processor webhooks are accepted directly.

post.summary: Register an RFID token and return it
post.description: Requires tokens:write (tenant-admin). Synchronous; replays with the same Idempotency-Key return the same token. A value is unique per tenant regardless of case and type (token_exists, with the existing token_id); the same value in another tenant is that tenant's own token. Values of the form iv + 18 hex digits, remotestart-<n> or PAY_<n> are reserved for payment flow charging tokens (token_reserved). An ISO14443 value (the default type) is 8 or 14 hex digits and an ISO15693 value 16, as the charging core checks them (token_format_invalid).

post.summary: Search the tenant's RFID tokens
post.description: Requires tokens:read. Read-only, so it takes no Idempotency-Key. The filters of GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/tokens (id_token, external_reference, status, type, after, limit) in a JSON body, with the same results: a card's value stays out of the URL, and so out of proxy and access logs. id_token matches case-insensitively, as chargers are authorized.

patch.summary: Block, unblock, expire or relabel a token
patch.description: Requires tokens:write (tenant-admin). Synchronous; changes only the supplied fields, and null clears expires_at, label or external_reference. Blocked and Expired make the core refuse the card at the next authorization. The value and type are immutable. Payment flow charging tokens answer token_not_found.

post.summary: Import RFID tokens from JSON or CSV

Up to 5,000 rows as JSON {"rows": [...]} or text/csv with a header row (id_token, type, status, expires_at, label, external_reference); at most 1 MiB. Rows match existing tokens by external_reference, else by id_token (case-insensitive): new values are created, given fields of existing ones updated, others reported unchanged, so re-running a file is safe. Absent fields keep their current value (new tokens: ISO14443, Accepted); a new ISO14443 value must be 8 or 14 hex digits and an ISO15693 value 16 (row code token_format_invalid). dry_run=true validates and plans without writing and needs no Idempotency-Key. Invalid rows are reported per row and skipped; valid rows still apply. A 503 outcome_unknown leaves some rows applied: re-run the same file with a new key.

get.description: One row per connector. A location's fields repeat on each of its rows (location_ref identifies it and becomes its external_reference); a charger's rows share its charger_id and an EVSE's connectors its evse_number. Required: location_ref, location_name, country, latitude, longitude, time_zone, charger_id, evse_number, connector_type. Units: max_voltage_v in V, max_amperage_a in A, max_power_w in W. Requires stations:read, or an API key holding migration:import (see the dry run).

post.summary: Dry-run a network import, or apply a dry run
post.description: Moves an existing network (locations, chargers as stations, their EVSEs and connectors) into the project. A dry run is the default: send text/csv (the template), or JSON {"source": "ocpi_locations"} with an OCPI 2.2.1 Locations document or a feed (the incumbent's Locations module URL and the token it issued you, read with GET requests only, over public https; the token is used for this request alone and never stored). At most 5,000 EVSEs, 20,000 source rows (CSV rows, or OCPI Locations and EVSEs) and 8 MiB. The answer (201) is the plan: every location and charger as create, update, skip or error with the reason (duplicates in the file, chargers that exist in this or another project, missing coordinates or time zone, unknown connector types, charger IDs that do not fit the project's rules). Nothing is written. Where the charger model library's import hints are on for the project (off by default; Ivora turns them on per environment or per project): where the source states a charger's vendor, model and firmware_version (CSV columns, or charger_map entries), its row carries the charger model library's match (model_profile), advisory risk_flags, and the values a verified profile knows for connector fields the source leaves empty (autofill.suggestions); autofill=apply writes those into the dry run (autofill.applied lists each one, connector_number included when autofill numbered a connector), never over a value the source gives; ?autofill= and an OCPI body's autofill that disagree are refused (422 invalid_request). Then POST again with apply=true and dry_run_id (no body, an Idempotency-Key): apply writes exactly what the dry run showed, in batches, and answers 200 with the station, location and connector IDs; 409 import_stale when the project changed since, with nothing written. After a 503 outcome_unknown or a partial import, apply again with a new key: it resumes. Chargers keep their own IDs: under the project's charger URL where per-project charger URLs are on (name p<tenant_id>-<charger_id>), else as global OCPP connection names. Once the global charger URL is closed to new registrations in an environment, a charger to create under a global name is an error row global_charger_url_retired and apply answers 409 global_charger_url_retired: staff turn per-project charger URLs on for the project first. No charger is contacted. Requires a team owner or admin of the project (projects:manage) signed in, or Ivora staff (signed in, or a staff key with stations:write), or an API key holding migration:import: a project key of this project (only the team's owners and admins, and Ivora administrators, grant that scope; developers cannot), or a team migration key of this project's active migration whose owner's role there holds it over every site. A key makes at most 10 dry runs and applies a minute (429 rate_limited with Retry-After). Each dry run and apply is audited (network_import.dry_run, network_import.applied) with the key and who made it. Only the dry run's maker applies it: the same key, or a signed-in member of the same team (403 forbidden otherwise). A team migration key made before keys reached these routes is refused (403 migration_key_refused): make a new one. Errors: 402 billing_suspended, 402 payment_method_required, 404 import_not_found, 409 global_charger_url_retired, 409 import_applied, 409 import_in_progress, 409 import_reverted, 409 import_stale, 409 request_in_progress, 409 self_serve_charger_cap, 413 request_too_large, 415 unsupported_media_type, 422 feed_failed, 422 feed_invalid, 422 feed_refused, 422 feed_too_large, 422 import_too_large, 503 outcome_unknown. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

post.summary: Show a text message on a charger screen
post.description: Synchronous desired state: stores the message and returns at once with status pending; Ivora pushes it on the next sweep and never waits for the charger. On OCPP 2.0.1 and 2.1 it is a SetDisplayMessage (priority, state, window and plain UTF8 text). OCPP 1.6 has no display message: it goes only through the charger's display adapter template when that has text messages, otherwise status unsupported with a reason and nothing is sent. Text over the adapter's per-line limit is refused with 422 message_too_long, never truncated. Plain text only: links, markup and control characters are 422. At most 10 messages per EVSE that have not ended (past ends_at). Replays with the same Idempotency-Key return the original result. Needs stations:write.

get.summary: Read a station's running cost setting and deliveries
get.description: enabled is true by default (source default) and follows an explicit choice once one is written (source manual, with updated_by and updated_at). support says how this charger's protocol receives cost: OCPP 1.6 by the Open Charge Alliance California Pricing DataTransfer (org.openchargealliance.costmsg RunningCost and FinalCost), OCPP 2.x by CostUpdated where this environment enables it, or charger_rejected when the charger refused the DataTransfer (rejection has its status and time). sessions lists the latest priced bills on the station with what the charging core accepted, and is null without billing:read.

put.summary: Switch running cost messages for a station on or off
put.description: On by default for every station; this stores an explicit choice that always wins over the default and persists until changed. When enabled, Ivora sends each bill started through this API its running cost while it charges (energy × the bill's rate, as finalization rounds it, at most every interval_seconds and only when it changed) and, on OCPP 1.6, its final cost once after it ends. Sessions without an Ivora bill get no message. Returns at once; the sweep sends. The charger must support the California Pricing extension (OCPP 1.6 CustomDisplayCostAndPrice) or CostUpdated; an OCPP 1.6 charger that rejects it reads charger_rejected and gets nothing until it reboots, and any write here clears that so the next session tries again. Replays with the same Idempotency-Key return the original result.

post.summary: Record a site flip of the project's migration
post.description: The project's charger proxy key (migration:proxy, made by Ivora administrators, bound to this project) or Ivora platform administrators; team roles and other keys are refused (tenants learn of flips through site.flipped, they do not declare them). The same flip as the staff route: the migration's charger proxy calls it after it moved a site's chargers. Emits site.flipped (direction to_ivora) or site.flip_rolled_back (to_previous_platform) to the project's webhooks with the location, its stations and their EVSEs, and records each moved station's route for QR sticker scans. It routes no charger. station_ids, when given, must all be at the location; otherwise every station there moved. Another project's location answers 404. Synchronous; replays with the same Idempotency-Key return the original result and emit nothing. Audit-logged (migration.site_flipped). Errors: 403 restricted_key_refused, 404 location_not_found, 409 station_in_shadow. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

get.summary: List the project's migrating chargers and where each is routed
get.description: The chargers the migration's charger proxy reports for this project, and those a site flip recorded: each one's route (ivora or previous_platform), the side its connection is open on, shadow mode, the recorded route QR scans follow, and its latest rollback with the reconnect status. Ordered by station ID; after is the last station ID of the previous page. Requires stations:read.

get.summary: Read one migrating charger
get.description: The same view as the list, for one station. Requires stations:read. Errors: 404 migration_charger_not_found, 404 station_not_found. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

post.summary: Roll a pilot charger back to the previous platform
post.description: Records a rollback that the charger proxy applies within seconds: it routes the charger back to the previous platform and closes its connection to Ivora, and the charger reconnects there by itself. Nothing is sent to the charger and nothing changes on Ivora's charging core. Always allowed, also while charging: a session running on Ivora then stays open on Ivora and is reconciled by hand. name must be the station's connection name (409 station_name_mismatch, details.name); reason is kept in the audit log and the event. Read the result and the reconnect status with GET .../migration/rollbacks/{rollback_id}; migration.charger_rolled_back is emitted once the proxy switched it and no connection to Ivora is open. Works while Ivora's charging core is unreachable (the station is read from the proxy's report). A rollback the proxy does not apply raises an on-call alert after ten minutes and expires after 24 hours; one Ivora staff moved forward again since is superseded. Needs stations:admin (team owners and admins, Ivora staff, API keys created with it). A retry with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same rollback, as it is now. Errors: 404 station_not_found, 409 migration_already_rolled_back, 409 migration_charger_not_proxied, 409 migration_rollback_pending, 409 station_name_mismatch. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

get.summary: Read a rollback and the charger's reconnect status
get.description: status: pending, applied_socket_open, applied, failed, superseded or expired. reconnect: whether the charger reconnected to the previous platform through the proxy. Requires stations:read. Errors: 404 migration_rollback_not_found. See [Errors and statuses](https://ivoracharge.co/developers/guides/reference/errors).

Each lookup counts in the scan counts (website_lookup_moved, website_lookup_stay or rate_limited).  Errors: 429 rate_limited. A session that started at most 30 days before it was received is recorded; one dated before the station was registered in the project, an older one, or one from a shadow period is refused (status refused, refused_reason) and kept here as evidence. transaction_id links the transaction the charging core saved, when it saved one: that transaction is billed like any other (a bill whose charging token it used settles it within its hold: automatic_billing), and on a roaming partner's token its CDR is sent with a remark that it was late, or held for staff when refused. A session the core did not save reaches no bill or CDR; review it and bill by hand where appropriate. Filters: station_id, kind (session, orphan_stop), status (recorded, refused).
